Putting It All Together 
The graph below summarizes the meaning of the 4 DRI values for nutrient intake. 
Figure 1.11. DRI values for nutrient intake. The EAR, RDA, AI, and UL are shown relative to the observed 
level of intake and risk of inadequacy and adverse effects. 
DEFINING NUTRIENT REQUIREMENTS: DIETARY REFERENCE INTAKES
39

Figure 1.11 Image Description 
The image is a line graph, with “observed level of intake” on the x-axis; “risk of inadequacy” 
on the left-hand y-axis; and “risk of adverse effects” on the right-hand y-axis. The graphed line 
is U-shaped, showing an increased risk of inadequacy at low levels of nutrient intake on the 
left side of the graph and increased risk of adverse effects at high levels of nutrient intake on 
the right side of the graph. Moving from left to right, lines are drawn representing the EAR 
(halfway on the slope of the left side of the U); RDA (at the base of the slope on the left side of 
the U); and UL (at the base of the slope on the right side of the U). The AI is shown as a range 
between the EAR and UL. 
This graph shows the risks of nutrient inadequacy and nutrient excess as we move from a low intake 
of a nutrient to a high intake. Starting on the left side of the graph, you can see that when you have a 
very low intake of a nutrient, your risk of nutrient deficiency is high. As your nutrient intake increases,
